newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-B.A.T year profits set to climb.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-B.A.T year profits set to climb.

text.p: B.A.T Industries should show healthy full year results of about 2.6 billion stg on Wednesday up from 2.44 billion last time helped by continued growth in cigarette sales and an improving financial services business.
Brokers' pretax, pre-exceptional profit forecasts range from 2.586 to 2.717 billion stg after exceptional items of about 80 million stg, but a pack are grouped around 2.6 billion to 2.65 billion.

Analysts have had to adjust their estimates repeatedly for the strength of sterling -- about 60 percent of BAT's earnings are in dollar related currencies with U.S. insurance subsidiary Farmers and tobacco firm Brown & Williamson contributing about $1.0 billion each to annual earnings.

The company said at the nine month stage that good progress in both its businesses is being maintained, with trading profit from financial services up three per cent to 846 million stg and tobacco profit ahead seven per cent to 1,265 million stg.

At the full year stage analysts are broadly looking for a 1.14 billion stg from financial services up from 1.052 billion stg, helped partly by new business growth at Farmer's and a much better performance from Allied Dunbar, and an eight percent increase in trading profit from tobacco to 1.67 billion.

At the nine month stage B.A.T reported general business profit was slightly up at 502 million, with growth at Farmers more than compensating for a reduction in UK composite insurer Eagle Star's profits which resulted from a strengthening of environmental reserves.
There was a sustained improvement in the life and investment business, although this is not yet fully reflected in the 5 percent increase in profit to 344 million stg, said the company.

The groups Allied Dunbar Assurance subsidiary reported double digit increases in both single and regular premiums in 1996. Total new business premiums -- new regular premiums plus one tenth of single premiums increased 19 percent to 257.8 million stg.

New single premiums rose 24 percent to 789.9 million stg while regular premiums were 17 percent ahead at 178.8 million stg. B.A.T Industries' pre-tax profit rose to 2,039 million, a nine per cent increase on last year's record first nine months.

Investors are likely to focus on hopes that B.A.T may yet be able to settle the growing number of legal claims in the U.S. over smoking related diseases. There is also interest in the company's plans for expansion in the emerging markets of the Far East and China.
"I think B.A.T's fortunes will still be significantly influenced by U.S. litigation," said Paribas analyst Tom Bennett. Paribas has a buy recommendation out on the stock.
The market range for the total dividend payout is 25.95p to 26.25p.
